history.dynasty: Ancient (2nd century AD legend); gateway inscriptions 8th-9th century
history.period: Legendary 2nd century AD (unverified); 8th-9th century epigraphical references
history.summary: Umamaheshwaram is an ancient Shiva temple in the Nallamala forest near Rangapur village, Achampet mandal, Nagarkurnool district. It is one of the four ancient dvaras (gateways) of Srisailam - the northern entrance - with epigraphical sources from the 8th-9th centuries; tradition holds a visit to Srisailam is incomplete without Umamaheshwaram. The Nagarkurnool district site records the temple's history as dating to the 2nd century AD, believed built during the reign of Maurya Chandragupta (unverified legend). The swayambhu linga is enshrined in a naturally formed cave, white on one side and red on the other; a huge tank stands near the temple. Hill ranges shield the temple and the 500-metre stretch to Papanasanam (the self-refilling spring) from sunlight most of the day, keeping temperatures cool year-round - the 'Poor Man's Ooty'. Perennial hillock water falls on the temple, likened to Goddess Ganga. BUILD-DATE CONFLICT (flag): district site says 2nd century AD; another account says 7th century CE/Rashtrakuta inscriptions - verify. OPENING-HOURS CONFLICT (flag): district site says 9:30 AM-4:00 PM daily; Telangana360 says 7 AM-8:30 PM - verify. CSV DISTRICT FLAG: CSV town/district field carries 'Mahbubnagar' (pre-2016 district); actual location is Umamaheshwaram near Rangapur, Achampet mandal, Nagarkurnool district.

name: Umamaheshwaram Temple
town_description: Umamaheshwaram is a hill shrine in the picturesque Nallamala forest ~4 km from Rangapur village, Achampet mandal, Nagarkurnool district, Telangana, ~100 km from Hyderabad on the Hyderabad-Srisailam highway (NH7). It is called the 'Poor Man's Ooty' for its year-round cool microclimate.

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~140 km).
travel.railway: Hyderabad Deccan is the nearest major railway station (~121 km).
travel.road: ~100 km from Hyderabad on the Hyderabad-Srisailam highway (NH7); ~4 km from Rangapur village near Achampet; ~51 km from Nagarkurnool. The last ~8 km is a steep ghat road with sharp curves.

visitor_information.opening_hours: 9:30 AM to 4:00 PM all days (district site - verify; another source says 7:00 AM to 8:30 PM).
